title: Metal-mediated weak adsorption enables the selective electrosynthesis of N-phenylhydroxylamine from nitrobenzene hydrogenation in water
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76066-6

The sustainable synthesis of N-phenylhydroxylamine (Ph-NHOH), a high-value intermediate, without over-hydrogenation side reactions is highly desirable. Here, the authors report the electrosynthesis of Ph-NHOH from nitrobenzene on metallic silver catalysts in aqueous media under ambient conditions.

title: Greenhouse warming exacerbates El Niño-induced Indian monsoon droughts
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76049-7

This study shows that greenhouse warming has strengthened the influence of El Niño on the Indian summer monsoon in the historical record and is projected to further intensify it, increasing risks of rainfall deficits and food insecurity in India.

title: Condensation of MATCAP promotes CENP-E-dependent chromosome congression in mitosis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75440-8

MATCAP catalyzes tubulin tyrosine code essential for microtubule dynamics. Here the authors show that MATCAP undergoes condensation to consolidate tubulin decoding with CENP-E motility to ensure a robust metaphase alignment during mitosis.

title: Effect of a complementary feeding intervention based on iron- and zinc-biofortified pearl millet on the gut microbiota in 12–18-month-old children: a randomized trial
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75674-6

In this randomized trial, the authors report that biofortified pearl millet is a potentially sustainable, climate-smart, and microbiome-friendly solution to improve micronutrient status in 12−18 month old children.

title: 3D-printed chiral luminous materials
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75988-5

Although 3D printing allows precise preparation of materials, it is challenging to prepare chiral materials by additive manufacturing. Here, the authors report a phase-separated polymerisation strategy that allows the preparation of 3D chiral luminous materials.

title: Ultrafast bimolecular reaction catalysis via engineered nuclear quantum effects in helium nanodroplets
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76012-6

Despite recent developments in ultrafast imaging, resolving how nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) influence chemical bond formation is still a major challenge. Here, the authors use femtosecond pump-probe spectroscopy to resolve NQEs in a light-induced bimolecular reaction within He nanodroplets, demonstrating environmental control over catalytic effects.

title: Gene regulatory innovations from transposable elements in primate cerebellum development
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75700-7

The roles of transposable elements in primate brain development remain underexplored. Here, the authors identify transposable elements with ancestral regulatory potential that have been co-opted as cis-regulatory elements in primates.

title: Losartan and prednisolone for post-COVID syndrome and cardiac inflammation: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75991-w

Persistent cardiac symptoms are common in post-COVID syndrome. In the Myoflame-19 trial, losartan plus prednisolone yielded neutral results for the primary outcome, change in left ventricular ejection fraction, in 279 participants with inflammatory cardiac involvement assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance.
